_note: This file is the single source of truth for what ships to deployment host. scripts/compile_skill_release.mjs reads every list below; it holds no duplicate hardcoded set. script_allowlist is the transitive import closure of script_entry_points and is verified against a freshly computed closure on every compile — a disagreement fails the build rather than shipping a package that cannot resolve. python_module_allowlist is the same statement for every Python runtime module, computed by the same both-directions rule from an `ast` walk rather than a regex.

_entry_point_note: Thirty-nine JavaScript entry points, none assumed discoverable from all the others. The vNext controller owns raw evidence through delivery and seals one model-first authority resolution; run_broker_intake.mjs owns the visible Brokers upload-or-skip checkpoint before raw-evidence compilation; run_structural_ownership_preflight.mjs is the installed pre-descendant topology gate invoked by the attachment controller before broker or debt work; v64's user-flow controller remains its workbook-stage delegate and rollback route. migrate_run_carrier.mjs is the explicit workspace-token-authorized carrier migration route. Constitution, terminal-exit, dynamic-concept, fault-injection, universal-matrix and raw-input canary entry points are release proofs rather than alternate user routes. The declared-evidence, filings and case-source entry points remain independently runnable diagnostics. inspect_workbook_semantics.mjs and validate_local_workbook_review.mjs independently bind the portable Phase-13 workbook evidence; verify/recalc_second_opinion.mjs independently binds the emitted and raw LibreOffice cache maps before terminal patching.

vendored_dependencies.name: jszip
vendored_dependencies.reason: The only third-party runtime dependency. The four portable validators read raw OOXML through it.
vendored_dependencies.note: Shipped as the pre-built UMD bundle so the vendored copy has no transitive dependencies of its own. It sits at node_modules/jszip because that is where Node resolves a bare specifier; the shipped validators are byte-identical to their local sources and must stay that way for source parity.

_python_note: The Python runtime modules ship alongside the JavaScript closure. They are held to the same standard: the closure is COMPUTED from python_entry_points by an ast walk (never a regex — this tree has docstring lines beginning `from ...` that a regex reads as imports) and compared with python_module_allowlist in both directions; a disagreement fails the build. Third-party imports are checked against allowed_python_third_party_imports exactly as a bare JS specifier is checked against allowed_bare_imports.
_python_entry_point_note: Twenty-nine Python entry points are independently runnable. run_attachment_evidence_pipeline.py is the sole raw-evidence transaction owner; broker, DCS and filings work is performed through subordinate runtime members, with public extractors, compilers, recovery tools and proposers retained as diagnostics. emit/__main__.py is the renderer CLI; prepare_local_workbook_review.py creates portable exact-workbook Phase-13 evidence without claiming native or human review; render and verify entry points provide independent structural, visual and financial proof.
_python_entry_point_notes_note: python_entry_point_notes is the exemption map for entry points that ship without a central user command. The broker components are intentionally subordinate diagnostics invoked by run_broker_pipeline.py; naming them as alternate user routes would recreate the sequencing defect the controller removes.

python_entry_point_notes.migrate_broker_run_state.py: Fail-closed, receipted migration of a sealed broker run across an intentional runtime-closure change; re-homes receipt-verified checkpoints and preserves exhaustion history so a live run resumes without losing progress or re-uploading sources. Invoked only on controller upgrades, never in ordinary runs.
python_entry_point_notes.run_attachment_evidence_pipeline.py: The sole raw-attachment evidence transaction owner; it sequences the broker and DCS controllers, case-source proposal and sealed ingress compilation.
python_entry_point_notes.run_dcs_pipeline.py: Invoked by run_attachment_evidence_pipeline.py as the resumable DCS checkpoint; independently runnable for diagnostics.
python_entry_point_notes.extract_filing_statements.py: Invoked by run_filings_pipeline.mjs as the native raw-filing extraction checkpoint; independently runnable for diagnostics.
python_entry_point_notes.propose_dcs_crosswalk.py: Invoked by run_dcs_pipeline.py to author a deterministic source-cell crosswalk after export basis is known; independently runnable for diagnostics.
python_entry_point_notes.extract_broker_evidence.py: Invoked by run_broker_pipeline.py as the raw evidence checkpoint; retained independently runnable for diagnostics, never as an alternate user route.
python_entry_point_notes.compile_broker_surface_census.py: Invoked by run_broker_pipeline.py as the independent coverage checkpoint; retained independently runnable for diagnostics.
python_entry_point_notes.compile_broker_vision.py: Invoked by run_broker_pipeline.py for two-read reconciliation and bounded cell adjudication; retained independently runnable for diagnostics.
python_entry_point_notes.verify_broker_semantics.py: Invoked by run_broker_pipeline.py as an independent semantic gate; retained independently runnable for diagnostics.
python_entry_point_notes.compile_broker_pack.py: Invoked by run_broker_pipeline.py only after prior broker checkpoints pass; retained independently runnable for diagnostics.
python_entry_point_notes.broker_period_recovery.py: Invoked by run_broker_pipeline.py after physical capture to resolve rendered period headers or quarantine only unresolved columns; retained independently runnable for diagnostics.

python_entry_point_notes.prepare_local_workbook_review.py: Local release-evidence utility. It leaves the attested workbook unchanged, creates a deterministic non-deliverable Show Formulas derivative, renders every visible sheet in both modes, and explicitly records human and native Excel review as not performed.
python_entry_point_notes.verify/broker_consensus_membership_oracl: Independent stdlib-only library/diagnostic invoked by the registered broker-consensus mutation harness. It ships as a separately smoke-tested verifier, not as an ordinary company-run command.
python_entry_point_notes.verify/forecast_ownership_physical_oracl: Invoked only by the controlled Stage-4 release orchestrator after portable emission and before recalculation or publication; independently binds the solver and expected C contract to raw workbook OOXML.

python_entry_point_smoke._note: What running each entry point from the clean release root must produce. Exit status alone is not the contract: two of these treat --help as an unrecognised argument and exit 1 with a usage line, and an entry point that had lost its imports would also exit non-zero. The required substring is what separates the two.

openpyxl.reason: The renderer writes the workbook through openpyxl. deployment host ships 3.1.5 natively. Vendoring it would put a second copy on sys.path ahead of or behind the native one depending on resolution order, which is how a version conflict gets shipped rather than avoided; a vendored 3.1.x that disagreed with the native one about style deduplication would move bytes the determinism gate compares.

fitz.reason: PyMuPDF reads the rendered PDF back. Native in deployment host. It is a compiled extension — vendoring it would mean shipping a platform-specific binary wheel, which the release format has no way to pin honestly across architectures.

PIL.reason: Pillow rasterises for the baseline image comparison. Native in deployment host; compiled extension, same vendoring objection as PyMuPDF.

numpy.reason: Pixel-array arithmetic for the baseline diff. Native in deployment host; compiled extension.

jsonschema.reason: emit/plan.py prefers jsonschema when importable and falls back to a deliberately small draft-07 subset when it is not, so the renderer still fails closed without it. required_at is runtime_optional and the compiler asserts the import really is guarded — an unguarded jsonschema import would turn a documented fallback into a hard dependency.

pdfplumber.reason: Optional local diagnostic PDF reader used only when PyMuPDF is unavailable. The deployment host production route remains PyMuPDF; absence of this fallback does not weaken or redirect that route.

pypdf.reason: Optional companion to pdfplumber for the local Poppler diagnostic path. It is not used by the deployment host PyMuPDF production route.

reportlab.reason: Synthetic-PDF dependency of the render-check self-test only. It is not on the end-user workbook build or PyMuPDF comparison path.

_python_vendoring_policy: Every entry above is provision=native and vendoring=forbidden, and the compiler enforces both: it refuses any provision other than native, and refuses to ship a vendored_dependencies entry whose name collides with a Python third-party root. None of these packages is vendored. Vendoring a package the host already provides is how you ship a version conflict.

prepare_local_workbook_review.py.reason: The portable Phase-13 evidence producer delegates only to the existing render package, never to the emitter or finance verifier. Its own OOXML derivative logic is standard-library only, while the renderer retains its declared PDF geometry and raster dependencies.

migrate_broker_run_state.py.reason: The fail-closed broker run migration tool is stdlib-only; it reuses run_broker_pipeline's digest primitives so a migrated checkpoint is sealed by byte-identical rules, and it authors no evidence of its own.

extract_filing_statements.py.reason: The raw-filings extractor is a subordinate runtime module that uses native PyMuPDF only for readable PDF text geometry and emits deterministic source-owned statement facts for the sealed filings lane.

propose_dcs_crosswalk.py.reason: The deterministic DCS crosswalk proposer is stdlib-only and maps sealed source cells under an explicit export-basis declaration before independent compilation and verification.

workflow_state.py.reason: The Python workflow-state helper is stdlib-only and enforces the same typed transition and blocker-ownership contract as the JavaScript controller layer.

archive_broker_pages.py.reason: The archive-only broker page renderer uses deferred native PyMuPDF to create screenshot evidence. It has no semantic or selected-cell authority, and callers degrade safely when rendering is unavailable.

zero_broker_authority.py.reason: The terminal optional-broker fallback is stdlib-only. It rewrites only the broker authority projection to a schema-valid zero-authority state while preserving immutable archive custody.

run_attachment_evidence_pipeline.py.reason: The top-level evidence controller is stdlib-only and sequences sealed subordinate lanes; optional archive rendering is delegated to archive_broker_pages rather than sharing extraction implementation.

run_dcs_pipeline.py.reason: The resumable DCS controller is stdlib-only and owns orchestration rather than source parsing or semantic verification.

run_broker_pipeline.py.reason: The broker controller is stdlib-only and sequences hash-bound evidence compilers without sharing their extraction or semantic implementation.

broker_terminal_recovery.py.reason: The broker terminal-recovery helper is stdlib-only and proves negative model consumption from immutable candidate cells and the canonical metric dictionary; it neither reads PDFs nor authors visual or semantic judgments.

pre_broker_demand.py.reason: The shared pre-broker demand normalizer is stdlib-only and reduces a sealed demand graph to the canonical broker-independent material states without reading source documents or authoring evidence.

broker_work_graph.py.reason: The broker work-graph helper is stdlib-only and records append-only task, checkpoint and execution-receipt lineage without reading source documents or authoring evidence.

broker_period_recovery.py.reason: The period-header recovery helper is stdlib-only. It binds model-host transcription to preserved rendered artifacts and otherwise quarantines only the unresolved columns.

broker_table_engine.py.reason: The provider-neutral adapter is stdlib-only and discovers optional host engines without importing or bundling them; normalized output still passes through the independent broker reconciliation gates.

extract_broker_evidence.py.reason: Broker evidence extraction prefers native PDF and workbook structure, preserves images, and defers every host-provided compiled dependency until the matching source type is encountered.

compile_broker_vision.py.reason: The image-consensus compiler is stdlib-only so verification cannot depend on the extractor's PDF or image implementation.

compile_broker_pack.py.reason: The broker crosswalk compiler is stdlib-only and operates only on already verified evidence artifacts.

broker_dynamic_concepts.py.reason: The run-scoped broker concept validator is stdlib-only and independently enforces the one-run insertion contract shared by compiler and semantic verifier.

broker_numeric.py.reason: Shared broker numeric parsing is stdlib-only and provides one deterministic locale-aware value grammar to extraction, period recovery and terminal reconciliation.

delivery_constitution.py.reason: The Python delivery-ownership helper is stdlib-only and loads the same immutable BLOCK / ASK / DEGRADE / LOG constitution as the public JavaScript controller.

compile_broker_candidate_manifest.py.reason: The immutable broker candidate-universe compiler is stdlib-only and cannot inherit reviewer-authored semantic classifications.

compile_broker_canonical_tables.py.reason: The canonical broker-table compiler is stdlib-only and reconciles already captured native and vision contributors.

compile_broker_surface_census.py.reason: The independent broker whole-surface census compiler is stdlib-only and recomputes coverage from hash-bound capture artifacts.

verify_broker_semantics.py.reason: The broker semantic oracle is stdlib-only and deliberately shares no compiler implementation with the broker-pack compiler.

extract_dcs_evidence.py.reason: The lossless DCS extractor is stdlib-only and reads CSV, JSON and OOXML directly into a source-owned cell ledger.

compile_dcs_evidence.py.reason: The DCS term-authority compiler is stdlib-only and operates only on sealed source tables, the immutable manifest and a reviewed cell crosswalk.

emit.reason: The renderer's job is to write a workbook. openpyxl expresses most of it; the terminal patch in emit/patch.py handles what openpyxl cannot.

verify.reason: STDLIB ONLY, and the compiler enforces it rather than trusting the docstring. Two separate claims: (a) a validator with no third-party surface has no version to disagree about, which is the point of the port off private workbook library; (b) the validator is the independent checker of what emit writes, so it must not reach into emit for anything. Both are checked on every compile — an import of openpyxl, or of emit, anywhere under verify/ fails the build.

render.reason: The image-check stage reads the rendered PDF, not the workbook object model, so it has no use for openpyxl and render/xlsx_model.py says so explicitly. Kept out of emit and verify so a render change cannot move either of them.

experience_trace.py.reason: The controller experience-trace helper is stdlib-only and records wall-clock ownership spans without reading or interpreting financial evidence.

rebind_broker_native_preflight.py.reason: The native-preflight rebinder is stdlib-only at its own boundary; it reuses already-declared broker extraction helpers and either proves exact source/demand compatibility or falls back to the ordinary full extraction path.

readers.verify/xlsx.py: 327 lines. Read-only. Extracts cached values, formulas, sheet names and value matches with semantics matched to private workbook library by probe. stdlib zipfile + ElementTree.
readers.render/xlsx_model.py: 697 lines. Read plus a page-setup patcher that always writes a separate copy. Carries an Excel LAYOUT model — column-width-to-pixel conversion against the default font's max digit width, row heights, print setup, conditional-format geometry. stdlib zipfile + ElementTree.
readers.emit/patch.py: 456 lines. Not a reader in the same sense: a byte-level rewriter of the .xlsx zip. Uses a hand-written tag scanner rather than ElementTree ON PURPOSE, because ElementTree does not round-trip bytes and this stage must not re-escape a quotation mark that needs no escaping between tags.

xlsx_reader_consolidation_decision.note_on_the_brief: The brief describes two independent readers. There are three. emit/patch.py is the third and is the one whose consolidation would cost the most.
reasons_to_keep_separate: The validator must not depend on openpyxl OR on emit, so that a bug in a shared reader cannot make the emitter and its own checker agree. verify/ reads back exactly what emit/patch.py writes: a shared misunderstanding of, say, t="str" versus t="s" would be invisible to a comparison performed through the same code. This is now enforced, not merely asserted — python_package_dependency_policy.verify forbids the import and the compiler fails the build on it.

They read different things. verify/xlsx.py wants values and formulas; render/xlsx_model.py wants geometry. Merging would make the validator carry ~700 lines of layout model it never calls, enlarging the audit surface of the one component whose small surface is the point.

Certification coupling. The closure hash covers every shipped file. A shared module would put a render-geometry tweak inside the validator's certified closure, so every change to column-width handling would invalidate the validator's certification and force a re-run of solver parity that nothing about the change could have affected.
emit/patch.py is byte-exact by requirement and the other two are not. Its escaping behaviour is load-bearing for the determinism and golden-file gates, which compare bytes.
xlsx_reader_consolidation_decision.cost_if_consolidated: One shared ooxml module of roughly 800-1000 lines plus three adapters, serving three incompatible policies (stdlib-only for verify, openpyxl-permitted for emit, byte-exact round-trip for patch). It would need re-certification of all three packages, and it would permanently couple the validator's certified closure to the renderer's. The saving is real but small: the genuine overlap is address parsing, shared-string resolution and namespace constants, on the order of 120 lines, none of it the part that is hard to get right.
xlsx_reader_consolidation_decision.revisit_if: verify/ ever needs layout geometry, or a defect is found in the address/shared-string handling of more than one of the three. Either would mean the duplication has started costing correctness rather than lines.

python_runtime.minimum_version_reason: verify/ declares 3.9+. The packages use `from __future__ import annotations` throughout, so PEP 585/604 spellings in annotations are strings and do not raise on 3.9.
python_runtime.smoke_interpreter_requirement: The chosen interpreter must satisfy every third-party package declared required_at=import, otherwise the smoke test cannot prove the package imports and the build fails rather than reporting a pass it did not earn. Candidates are tried in order and the rejection reason for each is recorded in the release manifest.

external_binaries.name: soffice
external_binaries.reason: render/soffice.py resolves soffice/libreoffice from SOFFICE_BIN or a fixed candidate list and returns BLOCKED — never a warning — when it is absent. Not required for import, so its absence does not affect the smoke test; render/selftest.py exists precisely so the checks remain provable without it.

_removed_strip_rules.local-plan-extractor-name: Removed on 2026-07-27, not weakened. It rewrote the single sentence naming `extract_plan.mjs`; that sentence now sits inside the block two-build-paths-subsection removes wholesale, so the rule would match zero times and fail its own exactly_one declaration. The invariant it protected — no bare `extract_plan.mjs` surviving into the compiled instructions — is asserted independently, and more strongly, by the dangling-script-reference check, which resolves bare filenames against the shipped basenames and fails the build on any that do not resolve. Restore this rule if the extractor is ever named outside that block.
